title: Close the tenant feature out: fix the remaining defects, restore a clean acceptance state, and prove multi-tenant mode is usable with E2E and smoke evidence
goal: The 2026-10-13 tenant packets landed the isolation work but left it uncommitted alongside three named defects (A: login-page picker blocked by tenantId's double semantics; B: /auth/tenants/current disagreeing with /auth/tenants/switchable on role/isActive; C: hard-deleting a tenant leaving Casbin domain policies) and a dev database polluted with fixture tenants whose stray memberships put the login picker in front of the platform operator. This task assessed that state against a live stack, fixed the one remaining code defect, documented the ops defect, restored a clean acceptance state, and ran the end-to-end and smoke suites on the real backend + MySQL + Redis + Chromium so that a human reviewer finds multi-tenant mode genuinely usable.
findings: A1 (assessment): defect A was ALREADY FIXED in the uncommitted worktree. login_service.findCredentialByUsername now tries the named tenant first and falls back to the global lookup, so the picker path reaches GateSessionIssuance instead of dying with 401. Re-verified live: selecting the member-only tenant returns 200 success (previously 401 user.login.error.not_found). No change made.

A2 (assessment): defect B was STILL PRESENT and was fixed here. GET /auth/tenants/current returned role='' and isActive=false for a tenant whose /auth/tenants/switchable entry reported role='owner' and isActive=true. GetCurrentTenant now resolves the caller's own active membership for the resolved tenant and reports its role with isActive=true, so the two endpoints agree (contract §2.2). No new authority: it reports what tenant_memberships already grants.

A3 (assessment): defect C was STILL ABSENT from the ops docs and was documented here. casbin_rule has no FK to tenants and the application has no purge path, so a hard delete leaves role:<key>@tenant:<id> grants behind; if the tenants AUTO_INCREMENT recycles the id, the next tenant inherits the old one's authority. Observed live: after the browser spec soft-deleted its tenant, 6 tenant-domain policies remained. docs/runbooks/TENANT_TROUBLESHOOTING.md gains §2b with the full procedure and verification queries, and its stale /api/v1/tenants endpoints were corrected to /api/v1/system/tenant.

A4 (assessment, acceptance-blocking): the dev database was polluted. ~45 leftover probe/e2e fixture tenants, orphan tenant-scoped users in soft-deleted tenants, and stray active memberships for the platform admin. The last one is what a human would actually notice: with memberships present, POST /auth/login for admin returns tenantSelectionRequired and NO token cookie, so the operator gets the picker instead of the console. All fixture rows were purged across the 18 tenant_id tables plus casbin_rule, and the acceptance state was verified clean: tenant_mode=multi, 0 active memberships, 0 fixture tenants, 0 tenant-domain policies, 40 platform policies.

A5 (assessment): the go vet / go test blocker recorded by both 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14 as not-run (any fresh Go tool invocation blocked indefinitely; 0.03s user CPU over 5 minutes) is GONE in this session. go vet ./modules/auth/login/... ./pkg/tenant/... and the matching go test both pass, so those recorded environment exceptions are closed for the packages this work touches.

S1 (stale fixture, discovered by running it): the tenant hostile browser matrix cannot pass. frontend/scripts/tenant-matrix-fixture-setup.mjs and the three tenant-hostile/tenant-protected specs log the platform admin in with an explicit tenantId against tenants 101/202. Before the isolation change the platform admin's global /api/v1/* policy still applied in-tenant; now a tenant-claim session resolves roles inside the tenant (contract §4), so a platform admin owning no tenant role gets an empty role set and every call is 403 permission.denied. Reproduced by hand: POST /auth/login {username:admin,password:123456,tenantId:101} yields 200 with roles:[] and perms containing platform:dashboard:*, and the next GET /system/dict/type/list returns code 403 permission.denied. Recorded as an explicit gap with a fix path (provision each fixture tenant via POST /system/tenant and log in as its own admin - the pattern the passing viewpoint spec uses) rather than rushed into this pass, because it also needs a decision about how fixture-written policies reach the running Casbin enforcer. The CI job smoke-tenant is continue-on-error, which is why this has been invisible to merge gates.

S2 (product question surfaced by S1): a platform-capable subject that names a tenant at login (or picks one from the picker) receives a session whose roles are resolved tenant-scoped, i.e. empty for a platform-only operator, so it lands in a console it cannot use. Whether a platform-capable subject should retain platform roles inside a tenant claim is a contract-level product decision.

S3 (open decision): docs/TENANT_SCOPE_FREEZE_DECISION_2026-10-15.md §6 - whether system_role / system_menu / system_permission are tenant-owned or globally shared - is still unruled. The shipped implementation is per-tenant roles plus global menus/permissions, which is the combination every probe in this pass validates; the document recommends moving roles back to global. Maintainer call.
